Research & Engineering Lineage · BWP-L1

Evolved Business Process Management

Business Process Management connects process purpose, evidence about actual work, legitimate change and observed consequences. Its scientific predicate is not the possession of a process map, owner title or maturity score. Those artefacts matter when they perform a justified function for a real recipient and decision.

Historical property reader: all 73 original rows from the immutable public predecessor are reproduced below. The current separately qualified study has its own exact subject and protected scientific interpretation. This page is not the current corrected source body.

BWP family and fourth-stage synthesis · Programme and state boundaries

Tradition and genealogy

The public predecessor describes a plural genealogy: industrial engineering and quality management; BPR and cross-functional redesign; office-information and workflow systems; representation, analysis and enactment; organisational capabilities and governance; and newer responsible, flexible and sustainability-oriented approaches. It distinguishes documented influence from shared ancestry and analytical reconstruction. “Evolved Business Process Management” is the packet’s analytical label, not the name of a universally recognised historical school.

Predicates and composition

The historical account distinguishes warranted understanding, legitimate and feasible action, and observed consequences. Purpose and beneficiaries determine a proportionate material boundary. Triangulated accounts of performed work qualify a representation. A representation must fit its communication, analysis or execution use. Effective authority, resources and knowledge qualify who can act. Plural outcome measures and a justified comparison qualify what can be claimed about improvement. A valid diagram does not settle organisational truth; deployment does not settle recipient benefit.

The public within-lineage composition permits evidence, exception and outcome feedback to reopen earlier decisions. It preserves lightweight stewardship, structured repeatable work, case-oriented professional work, negotiated inter-organisational work and evidence-intensive decision support as alternative configurations. Formal checking, simulation, automation or a new governance arrangement needs a real trigger. A concise shared account and a capable existing actor can be adequate.

Counterexamples, negatives and alternatives

A department can reduce its local handling time while moving delay or burden to another actor. A readable process model can support discussion while lacking an execution contract. A workaround can expose a real mismatch while also evading a necessary control. These distinctions explain why purpose, evidence, authority and consequence require separate questions.

The public predecessor contains 73 property candidates: 58 conditionally usable, fourteen non-retained and one unresolved. Its 48 source records are not 48 independent effectiveness experiments. Its longitudinal example preserves 25 intended processes in ten organisations, seven implemented processes in five organisations, and five raw lead-time improvements versus two deteriorations. Those nested and context-dependent populations establish neither universal benefit nor a general failure rate. EBPM-053 remains a historical unresolved candidate; a goal prompt supplies no organisational authority.

These historical statements are sourced to the published intake, full report, composition/genealogy model and source table. Historical assertions are preserved without presenting them as the corrected current frontier.

Lineage class

NATIVE_WITH_ANALYTICAL_REFINEMENT

Original form

Organise work around outcomes received by a customer rather than departmental tasks.

Problem it addressed

Identify a defensible unit of end-to-end work and its purpose before intervening.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

A powerful buyer captures the purpose definition; broad aspirations are too vague to evaluate.

Mechanism

Identify the intended result, its recipients and the end-to-end work that produces it. Make competing outcome claims visible before choosing measures or redesigning tasks; a purchaser’s preference is not automatically every affected person’s interest.

Trigger or context

A process is being selected, assessed or changed and local success may differ from the received outcome.

Non trigger or cheap path

For a small, already understood service, a short agreed purpose and completion statement plus sample cases is sufficient; no portfolio exercise is required.

Dependencies or preconditions

An identifiable beneficiary or affected constituency; a feasible way to resolve competing objectives; evidence of actual results.

Domain profile
Process purpose and boundary

The work from a meaningful initiating need to a received result, with explicit exclusions.

Beneficiaries and affected actors

Customers or service recipients, frontline workers, upstream/downstream participants and indirectly affected people.

Work as described versus work as performed

Compare the declared purpose with representative received results and complaints; a purpose statement alone is not evidence of fulfilment.

Model purpose and abstraction

Purpose statement, case examples and an outcome/actor map; a flow diagram is optional.

Performance or outcome measure

Received outcome and burdens, not merely completed activities.

Redesign hypothesis and causal limit
Hypothesis

Identify the intended result, its recipients and the end-to-end work that produces it. Make competing outcome claims visible before choosing measures or redesigning tasks; a purchaser’s preference is not automatically every affected person’s interest.

Causal limit

S030 supplies a normative challenge to efficiency-only objectives; analytically, naming a customer does not justify excluding non-paying affected people.

Process owner and effective authority

Responsible managers can commit resources; beneficiaries and affected workers contribute outcome evidence. Analysts cannot decide whose interests prevail merely by drawing the boundary.

Human discretion and exception handling

Discretion may be necessary to achieve the purpose when a rule’s normal conditions fail.

Automation and external effect boundary

Automation must be judged against the same received outcome and affected parties.

Feedback and revision trigger

Changed beneficiary needs, complaints, displaced harm or new strategic commitments.

Expected engineering payoff
Intended postcondition

A proposed change can be judged against an explicit outcome and identified recipients, rather than only a department’s activity count.

Payoff status

Conditional expected payoff or rejected-claim boundary, not a universal observed effect size.

Decision

Original form

Cross-functional and interorganisational process boundaries correct fragmented local optimisation.

Problem it addressed

Identify a defensible unit of end-to-end work and its purpose before intervening.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Boundary expansion becomes endless; an aggregate hides a harmed subgroup; partners conceal costs.

Mechanism

Trace consequential work, waiting and risk beyond the unit receiving the improvement credit. Compare the whole affected path and require an explicit account of costs displaced onto partners, customers or unlogged workers.

Trigger or context

A local measure improves, work is outsourced, or a redesigned interface changes another actor’s burden.

Non trigger or cheap path

Inspect a few complete cases and ask receiving participants what changed. A full network model is unnecessary when interfaces and effects are simple.

Dependencies or preconditions

Access to receiving-side evidence or an explicit evidence limit; comparable case scope; identified boundary responsibilities.

Domain profile
Process purpose and boundary

Local process plus materially affected upstream, downstream and external interfaces.

Beneficiaries and affected actors

The unit claiming benefit and the parties whose time, risk or unpaid work may increase.

Work as described versus work as performed

Inspect receiving-side cases and off-system effort; do not infer absence from missing local logs.

Model purpose and abstraction

Interface/burden map at the level needed for the intervention, not a complete enterprise model.

Performance or outcome measure

Total elapsed time, risk and workload by affected party and case class.

Redesign hypothesis and causal limit

A local owner may change its own work but cannot bind a partner unilaterally. Cross-boundary obligations require agreement with the actors bearing them.

External effects of automated handoffs remain in scope even when the local task reports success.

Excessive decomposition hides cross-cutting work; a reference model is mistaken for actual practice.

Represent process families, decomposition and interfaces at the abstraction needed for coordination. Preserve cross-cutting dependencies when decomposing and adapt reference architectures to actual work rather than treating a borrowed map as an empirical description.

Several processes share resources, objects or interfaces and local changes can conflict.

Criterion operative coupling
Criterion

An analyst can locate the affected process and its consequential relationships without equating reporting lines with work flow.

Operating method

Represent process families, decomposition and interfaces at the abstraction needed for coordination. Preserve cross-cutting dependencies when decomposing and adapt reference architectures to actual work rather than treating a borrowed map as an empirical description.

Communication

Local owners reconcile shared terms, boundaries and dependencies before treating components as independent.

Authority

Enterprise/process coordinators maintain the map with local expertise; the architecture does not override functional or contractual authority.

Consequence evidence

Validate architecture relationships against actual handoffs and shared work, not just approved documents. Measure: Dependency visibility and decision usefulness rather than diagram coverage.

Original form

Discovery gathers process information from actors and artefacts before analysis or redesign.

Problem it addressed

Establish what actual work the available accounts justify, including disagreement and omission.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Observation changes behaviour; workshop consensus conceals dissent; system logs omit essential coordination.

Mechanism

Compare interviews, documents, walkthroughs, direct observation and event evidence where they reveal different aspects of work. Record provenance and disagreement; neither a remembered account, a prescription nor an event log is intrinsically the whole truth.

Trigger or context

A decision depends on what actually happens and available accounts may be incomplete, selective or incentive-distorted.

Non trigger or cheap path

For a transparent low-risk process, a few representative walkthroughs with performers and recipients may suffice; all evidence channels are not compulsory.

Dependencies or preconditions

Access to relevant participants and cases; a sampling rationale; permission to observe work without disproportionate intrusion.

Process purpose and boundary

The performed work relevant to the proposed analysis, including off-system activities.

Frontline performers, recipients, analysts and less visible supporting participants.

Work as described versus work as performed

Explicitly distinguish prescribed, elicited, remembered, observed and logged accounts.

Coverage of consequential work and unresolved discrepancies, not interview counts.

Compare interviews, documents, walkthroughs, direct observation and event evidence where they reveal different aspects of work. Record provenance and disagreement; neither a remembered account, a prescription nor an event log is intrinsically the whole truth.

Automated records are one observation channel with instrumentation boundaries.

NATIVE_WITH_ANALYTICAL_REFINEMENT

Original form

As-is discovery must cope with variants and exceptional work, not only the normal path.

Problem it addressed

Establish what actual work the available accounts justify, including disagreement and omission.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Rare catastrophic cases disappear in averages; sampling only completed cases excludes abandonment.

Mechanism

Sample materially different case types, failure paths and informal coordination. State which variants are covered and which remain uncertain; do not infer that rare or unlogged work is irrelevant simply because it is absent from a convenient sample.

Trigger or context

Case mix, exceptions or hidden handoffs could change analysis or redesign conclusions.

Non trigger or cheap path

Use a few deliberately contrasting cases when the variant space is small; exhaustive enumeration is unnecessary.

Dependencies or preconditions

A risk-relevant variant distinction and access to at least some atypical cases or informed accounts.

Domain profile
Process purpose and boundary

Case classes, exceptions, abandoned work and informal coordination within the intervention scope.

Beneficiaries and affected actors

People whose cases differ from the dominant workflow and workers handling unusual demand.

Work as described versus work as performed

Separate observed frequency from plausible-but-unobserved exceptions and participant recollections.

Model purpose and abstraction

Variant table, exception examples or a richer process/case model when needed.

Performance or outcome measure

Coverage and harm by case class rather than only an aggregate mean.

Redesign hypothesis and causal limit
Hypothesis

Sample materially different case types, failure paths and informal coordination. State which variants are covered and which remain uncertain; do not infer that rare or unlogged work is irrelevant simply because it is absent from a convenient sample.

Causal limit

S014 and S041 demonstrate that routine models can omit consequential variation. Analytically, exhaustive variant modelling can cost more than responsive case handling.

Process owner and effective authority

Process investigators select cases with performers and recipients; owners accept the resulting uncertainty or commission further inquiry.

Human discretion and exception handling

Legitimate exceptional action is investigated on its purpose and constraints.

Automation and external effect boundary

Automation may cover only a declared subset of variants, with a usable manual route.

Feedback and revision trigger

New case mix, abandonment, recurring exception or an adverse outlier.

Expected engineering payoff
Intended postcondition

A redesign claim states the case classes it covers and the exceptions that could defeat it.

Payoff status

Conditional expected payoff or rejected-claim boundary, not a universal observed effect size.

Decision or consumer
Decision

Whether and how to apply the mechanism under its trigger, or reject its universalised use. Case mix, exceptions or hidden handoffs could change analysis or redesign conclusions.

Consumer and authority

Process investigators select cases with performers and recipients; owners accept the resulting uncertainty or commission further inquiry.

Actor and authority boundary

Process investigators select cases with performers and recipients; owners accept the resulting uncertainty or commission further inquiry.

Communication or interaction requirement

Communicate normal-path coverage separately from exception and missing-case coverage.

Observable postcondition

A redesign claim states the case classes it covers and the exceptions that could defeat it.

Known failure modes

Rare catastrophic cases disappear in averages; sampling only completed cases excludes abandonment.

Important criticisms

S014 and S041 demonstrate that routine models can omit consequential variation. Analytically, exhaustive variant modelling can cost more than responsive case handling.

How the property evolved

A normal-flow account is expanded only where consequential variants warrant it; uncertainty remains explicit.

Mature or evolved form

Sample materially different case types, failure paths and informal coordination. State which variants are covered and which remain uncertain; do not infer that rare or unlogged work is irrelevant simply because it is absent from a convenient sample.

Ceremony vs property
Protected function

A redesign claim states the case classes it covers and the exceptions that could defeat it.

Consumer

Process investigators select cases with performers and recipients; owners accept the resulting uncertainty or commission further inquiry.

Minimal adequate alternative

Use a few deliberately contrasting cases when the variant space is small; exhaustive enumeration is unnecessary.

Fuller form trigger

Case mix, exceptions or hidden handoffs could change analysis or redesign conclusions.

Prerequisites

A risk-relevant variant distinction and access to at least some atypical cases or informed accounts.

Simplification risk

Rare catastrophic cases disappear in averages; sampling only completed cases excludes abandonment.

Omission or retirement condition

Omit when the stated trigger is absent, an existing/cheaper mechanism supplies the required function, or its risk/consumer/dependency has disappeared. Reconsider on: New case mix, abandonment, recurring exception or an adverse outlier.

Anti ceremony boundary

Presence of an artefact, role, meeting, score or tool does not establish the observable postcondition; removing it must not destroy a real protective or accountability function.

NATIVE_WITH_ANALYTICAL_REFINEMENT

Original form

Guidelines recommend smaller, clearer, more structured process models.

Problem it addressed

Support the users’ consequential distinctions without confusing representation with reality or execution.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Decomposition hides cross-boundary dependencies; adherence to a size rule increases navigation cost.

Mechanism

Reduce unnecessary representational complexity while preserving decision-relevant behaviour and relationships. Test the simplified form with its users; use modularisation or multiple coordinated views when a single small diagram would conceal essential interactions.

Trigger or context

Users cannot reliably interpret a model, or model changes introduce structural errors.

Non trigger or cheap path

Remove an ambiguity or improve a label before imposing a new modelling standard or decomposition programme.

Dependencies or preconditions

A known task and user population; explicit behaviour or meaning to preserve; a comparison with the current representation.

Domain profile
Process purpose and boundary

The representation’s complexity relative to a specific user task.

Beneficiaries and affected actors

Model consumers and maintainers, including non-specialists.

Work as described versus work as performed

Simplification is checked against the underlying work/requirements rather than treated as discovery.

Model purpose and abstraction

Structured diagram, modular views or plain description selected by observed comprehension.

Performance or outcome measure

Interpretation errors, task time and maintenance burden with preserved meaning.

Redesign hypothesis and causal limit
Hypothesis

Reduce unnecessary representational complexity while preserving decision-relevant behaviour and relationships. Test the simplified form with its users; use modularisation or multiple coordinated views when a single small diagram would conceal essential interactions.

Causal limit

S010’s small guideline experiment did not establish the tested benefit; S044’s positive notation redesign has one-platform/cohort limits. Simpler-looking is not universally better.

Process owner and effective authority

Modellers propose changes; users and domain experts check that useful meaning has not been lost.

Human discretion and exception handling

Do not simplify away meaningful exceptions or decision authority.

Automation and external effect boundary

An equivalent communicative simplification is not necessarily executable-equivalent.

Feedback and revision trigger

Observed comprehension failures, growing model maintenance cost or changed user tasks.

Expected engineering payoff
Intended postcondition

Users handle the relevant cases at least adequately without loss of critical constraints or relationships.

Lineage class

NATIVE_WITH_ANALYTICAL_REFINEMENT

Original form

Clear activity labels, including verb–object conventions, aid process-model interpretation.

Problem it addressed

Support the users’ consequential distinctions without confusing representation with reality or execution.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Mechanical verb–object rewriting obscures accepted specialist terms; tidy labels conceal undefined responsibilities.

Mechanism

Use terms that distinguish what action or decision occurs and what object is affected, in the intended users’ language. Resolve ambiguous domain terms before standardising a label grammar; test important labels through concrete cases.

Trigger or context

Users disagree about an activity, decision or completion label, or labels are reused across roles.

Non trigger or cheap path

A brief glossary or example can be enough; a mandatory naming convention is unnecessary when existing terms work.

Dependencies or preconditions

Knowledge of the user vocabulary and the distinctions the model must communicate.

Domain profile
Process purpose and boundary

The meaning of actions, decisions and objects in a representation.

Beneficiaries and affected actors

People who interpret or execute labelled work, including external partners.

Work as described versus work as performed

Names are checked against actual activities and decision meanings, not only documents.

Model purpose and abstraction

Labels with examples or a lightweight glossary; no universal naming grammar.

Performance or outcome measure

Consequential interpretation errors rather than convention-compliance percentage.

Redesign hypothesis and causal limit
Hypothesis

Use terms that distinguish what action or decision occurs and what object is affected, in the intended users’ language. Resolve ambiguous domain terms before standardising a label grammar; test important labels through concrete cases.

Causal limit

S009’s recommendations and S044’s bounded usability evidence do not prove one grammatical pattern best for all cultures, languages or tasks.

Process owner and effective authority

Domain participants determine meaning; model maintainers ensure consistent use without overriding legitimate local terminology.

Human discretion and exception handling

Labels must not imply that an optional judgement is a mandatory automatic action.

Automation and external effect boundary

A human-readable label does not specify executable service semantics.

Feedback and revision trigger

Ambiguous use, a new audience or a term whose meaning changes with the process.

Expected engineering payoff
Intended postcondition

Critical labels support the intended action/object distinction across the relevant users.

Conditional expected payoff or rejected-claim boundary, not a universal observed effect size.

Consumer and authority

Actor and authority boundary

Domain participants determine meaning; model maintainers ensure consistent use without overriding legitimate local terminology.

Communication or interaction requirement

Ask users what a label authorises or predicts and reconcile materially different readings.

Observable postcondition

Critical labels support the intended action/object distinction across the relevant users.

Known failure modes

Mechanical verb–object rewriting obscures accepted specialist terms; tidy labels conceal undefined responsibilities.

Important criticisms

S009’s recommendations and S044’s bounded usability evidence do not prove one grammatical pattern best for all cultures, languages or tasks.

How the property evolved

Crosswalk worthy

True

Criterion operative coupling
Criterion

Critical labels support the intended action/object distinction across the relevant users.

Operating method

Use terms that distinguish what action or decision occurs and what object is affected, in the intended users’ language. Resolve ambiguous domain terms before standardising a label grammar; test important labels through concrete cases.

Communication

Ask users what a label authorises or predicts and reconcile materially different readings.

Authority

Domain participants determine meaning; model maintainers ensure consistent use without overriding legitimate local terminology.

Consequence evidence

Names are checked against actual activities and decision meanings, not only documents. Measure: Consequential interpretation errors rather than convention-compliance percentage.

Original form

Problem it addressed

Support the users’ consequential distinctions without confusing representation with reality or execution.

Ignored non-operational elements conceal human obligations; tool import succeeds while semantics differ.

Mechanism

Declare whether a model communicates, analyses or drives execution, and identify the additional implementation semantics and organisational arrangements needed to move between those uses. Keep engine events and real completion separate until their correspondence is demonstrated.

Trigger or context

A model is handed to implementers, imported into a tool or presented as evidence that a process operates correctly.

NATIVE_WITH_ANALYTICAL_REFINEMENT

Original form

Decision models can separate decision logic from process-flow presentation.

Problem it addressed

Support the users’ consequential distinctions without confusing representation with reality or execution.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

A well-formed rule table embeds an unjustified policy; a model prediction is mistaken for authorisation.

Mechanism

Where decision rules vary independently of routing, distinguish the information/rules used to decide from the actor authorised to decide and from the consequences of that decision. Keep a traceable connection between a decision model and the process consuming its result.

Trigger or context

Business decisions are obscured in flow diagrams, reused across processes or changed independently of task order.

Non trigger or cheap path

A decision table or explicit rationale can be sufficient; DMN is an option rather than an obligation.

Dependencies or preconditions

Identifiable decision inputs, policy meaning, accountable authority and consumers of the decision.

Domain profile
Process purpose and boundary

A decision’s inputs, policy, result, authorised actor and consuming process.

Beneficiaries and affected actors

Decision subjects, policy owners, decision makers and downstream implementers.

Work as described versus work as performed

Compare declared rules with actual decisions, exceptions and received consequences.

Model purpose and abstraction

Decision table/model linked to flow; DMN version semantics require separate verification if used.

Performance or outcome measure

Decision correctness under stated criteria, consistency and affected-person outcomes.

Redesign hypothesis and causal limit
Hypothesis

Where decision rules vary independently of routing, distinguish the information/rules used to decide from the actor authorised to decide and from the consequences of that decision. Keep a traceable connection between a decision model and the process consuming its result.

Causal limit

S013 was inspected only for specification identity. Detailed DMN semantics are not inferred; S030 supports the broader accountability concern, not a validated universal decision protocol.

A rule author or prediction service is not automatically the legitimate decision maker; accountable actors retain domain-specific authority.

Human discretion and exception handling

Discretion and override conditions must not be erased by extracting a rule model.

Automation and external effect boundary

Automated decision support is distinct from permission to impose its result.

Policy change, unexplained decisions, missing input or mismatch between modelled and actual authority.

Lineage class

NATIVE_WITH_ANALYTICAL_REFINEMENT

Original form

Knowledge-intensive work motivates case-oriented and declarative alternatives to exhaustive advance sequencing.

Problem it addressed

Support the users’ consequential distinctions without confusing representation with reality or execution.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Discretion becomes unaccountable; a constraint model is too difficult to understand; supposedly flexible tools impose hidden rigidity.

Mechanism

Select support according to what can be known in advance: goals and information needs, mandatory constraints, planned tasks or a stable flow. Allow structured sub-processes inside knowledge work and avoid making flexibility equivalent to the absence of guidance.

Trigger or context

Cases require changing knowledge, professional judgement or runtime planning that an exhaustive flow would distort.

Non trigger or cheap path

A shared case note, goal list and essential constraints can be enough without a case-management engine.

Dependencies or preconditions

Competent participants; intelligible goals/constraints; usable shared information and a way to recognise unresolved obligations.

Domain profile
Process purpose and boundary

Knowledge-intensive cases with changing plans and potentially stable sub-processes.

Beneficiaries and affected actors

Knowledge workers, case recipients, supporting specialists and accountable sponsors.

Work as described versus work as performed

Observe how knowledge and decisions actually evolve, not only prescribed task sequences.

Model purpose and abstraction

Case information/goals, discretionary plans, constraints or hybrid models.

Performance or outcome measure

Case outcomes, unresolved obligations and adaptation burden, not path conformance alone.

Redesign hypothesis and causal limit
Hypothesis

Select support according to what can be known in advance: goals and information needs, mandatory constraints, planned tasks or a stable flow. Allow structured sub-processes inside knowledge work and avoid making flexibility equivalent to the absence of guidance.

Causal limit

S014 is conceptual/illustrative and S012 normative. S042’s formal admissibility does not prove suitability for every knowledge worker. The formal checking mechanism is separately registered as EBPM-073.

Process owner and effective authority

Case workers plan within professional and organisational authority; system flexibility does not grant new powers.

Human discretion and exception handling

Discretion is substantive but bounded by competence, authority and protected obligations.

Automation and external effect boundary

Automation may support information and stable sub-processes without controlling the whole case.

Feedback and revision trigger

Decision or consumer

Consumer and authority

Procedural, case-oriented and declarative forms remain alternatives or bounded hybrids; no universal replacement is asserted.

Protected function

Participants can adapt the work while preserving essential obligations and keeping others informed.

Consumer

Case workers plan within professional and organisational authority; system flexibility does not grant new powers.

Minimal adequate alternative

A shared case note, goal list and essential constraints can be enough without a case-management engine.

Fuller form trigger

Cases require changing knowledge, professional judgement or runtime planning that an exhaustive flow would distort.

Prerequisites

Competent participants; intelligible goals/constraints; usable shared information and a way to recognise unresolved obligations.

Anti ceremony boundary

Separate elapsed time experienced by the case or recipient from active work effort and resource occupancy. Locate waiting, transfer and rework contributions before attributing delay to an actor or deciding which activity to accelerate.

Show the timeline and distinguish work, queueing, handoff and interruption interpretations.

Authority

Analysts interpret time evidence with performers; owners can change allocation or handoff arrangements within their authority.

Consequence evidence

Compare event timestamps with what the worker and recipient regard as actual activity and waiting. Measure: Elapsed duration, active effort, occupancy and rework separately.

Original form

Queueing and simulation analyse capacity, demand variability and bottlenecks.

Problem it addressed

Explain and assess process outcomes with appropriate measures and causal limits.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Average-rate assumptions hide bursts; human multitasking violates resource models; a bottleneck merely moves downstream.

Mechanism

Examine demand, service variation, shared capacity and allocation rules together before adding resources or seeking maximum utilisation. Use a queueing model or simulation only when its assumptions represent the relevant work; recheck the end-to-end constraint after a local change.

Trigger or context

Persistent queues, fluctuating demand or shared-resource contention dominate outcomes.

Non trigger or cheap path

A workload/timeline comparison and a bounded allocation trial may dominate building a detailed stochastic model.

Meaningful arrival/service observations, resource availability and allocation assumptions; an appropriate steady-state or transient scope.

Process purpose and boundary

Queues, shared resources and capacity across the affected end-to-end path.

Beneficiaries and affected actors

Waiting recipients, resource managers, workers and downstream teams.

Work as described versus work as performed

Observed allocation and interruptions may differ from nominal staffing or scheduled capacity.

Model purpose and abstraction

A simple workload model, queueing abstraction or simulation matched to the problem.

A feedback loop is labelled waste; work is shifted to the recipient; handoff elimination overloads one actor.

Mechanism

Trace how a handoff, missing information or rejected output generates delay and repeated work. Distinguish avoidable rework from necessary checking, learning or repair before changing task boundaries or removing feedback.

Trigger or context

Cases bounce between actors, repeatedly request information or suffer unexplained rejection/delay.

Non trigger or cheap path

Model purpose and abstraction

Trace how a handoff, missing information or rejected output generates delay and repeated work. Distinguish avoidable rework from necessary checking, learning or repair before changing task boundaries or removing feedback.

Original form

Process simulation compares hypothetical changes to a model of the process.

Problem it addressed

Explain and assess process outcomes with appropriate measures and causal limits.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Precisely wrong forecasts, warm-up mismatch, unrepresented work, narrow intervals with poor coverage and overfitting.

Mechanism

Calibrate the model to the relevant case mix, resource behaviour and current work state; validate predictions against observations and report uncertainty and sensitivity. Treat scenarios as conditional forecasts, not observed consequences of an intervention.

Trigger or context

Alternatives are costly or disruptive to test directly, or queues/current cases make short-term effects non-obvious.

Non trigger or cheap path

Use arithmetic, a case timeline or a limited real-world trial when these answer the decision adequately.

Dependencies or preconditions

A representationally adequate model, credible input data, an evaluation baseline and awareness of model/data drift.

Domain profile
Process purpose and boundary

The simulated case/resource system and the actual process to which a forecast is transferred.

Beneficiaries and affected actors

Decision makers and the workers/recipients bearing forecast-error costs.

Work as described versus work as performed

Check modelled state, timestamps and behaviour against real ongoing cases.

Model purpose and abstraction

Calibrated simulation with explicit alternative scenarios and uncertainty, not an animation alone.

Performance or outcome measure

Prediction error, interval coverage and decision sensitivity; outcome effects need later observation.

Redesign hypothesis and causal limit
Hypothesis

Calibrate the model to the relevant case mix, resource behaviour and current work state; validate predictions against observations and report uncertainty and sensitivity. Treat scenarios as conditional forecasts, not observed consequences of an intervention.

Causal limit

S018 finds a sharpness/coverage trade-off and assumes consistent complete event data; S027 could not validate all successful-process models. Simulation is not a causal substitute for the missing world.

Process owner and effective authority

Analysts own model assumptions; operational decision makers decide whether the conditional evidence justifies action.

Human discretion and exception handling

Human allocation, adaptation and exception behaviour are model assumptions, not constants by definition.

Automation and external effect boundary

Automated simulation or optimisation does not authorise deployment of its preferred alternative.

Feedback and revision trigger

Calibration failure, current-state mismatch, changed resources or outcome drift.

Expected engineering payoff
Intended postcondition

A simulation-supported choice includes an empirical calibration check and conditions under which the prediction is not relied upon.

Payoff status

Conditional expected payoff or rejected-claim boundary, not a universal observed effect size.

Decision

Whether and how to apply the mechanism under its trigger, or reject its universalised use. Alternatives are costly or disruptive to test directly, or queues/current cases make short-term effects non-obvious.

Consumer and authority

Analysts own model assumptions; operational decision makers decide whether the conditional evidence justifies action.

Actor and authority boundary

Analysts own model assumptions; operational decision makers decide whether the conditional evidence justifies action.

Communication or interaction requirement

Communicate the baseline, predicted range, uncertain assumptions and alternatives to those making the intervention decision.

Observable postcondition

A simulation-supported choice includes an empirical calibration check and conditions under which the prediction is not relied upon.

Known failure modes

Precisely wrong forecasts, warm-up mismatch, unrepresented work, narrow intervals with poor coverage and overfitting.

Important criticisms

S018 finds a sharpness/coverage trade-off and assumes consistent complete event data; S027 could not validate all successful-process models. Simulation is not a causal substitute for the missing world.

How the property evolved

Current-state and uncertainty-aware forms refine older simulation practice without eliminating epistemic uncertainty.

Mature or evolved form

Calibrate the model to the relevant case mix, resource behaviour and current work state; validate predictions against observations and report uncertainty and sensitivity. Treat scenarios as conditional forecasts, not observed consequences of an intervention.

Ceremony vs property
Protected function

A simulation-supported choice includes an empirical calibration check and conditions under which the prediction is not relied upon.

Consumer

Analysts own model assumptions; operational decision makers decide whether the conditional evidence justifies action.

Minimal adequate alternative

Use arithmetic, a case timeline or a limited real-world trial when these answer the decision adequately.

Fuller form trigger

Alternatives are costly or disruptive to test directly, or queues/current cases make short-term effects non-obvious.

Prerequisites

A representationally adequate model, credible input data, an evaluation baseline and awareness of model/data drift.

Simplification risk

Precisely wrong forecasts, warm-up mismatch, unrepresented work, narrow intervals with poor coverage and overfitting.

Omission or retirement condition

Omit when the stated trigger is absent, an existing/cheaper mechanism supplies the required function, or its risk/consumer/dependency has disappeared. Reconsider on: Calibration failure, current-state mismatch, changed resources or outcome drift.

Anti ceremony boundary

Presence of an artefact, role, meeting, score or tool does not establish the observable postcondition; removing it must not destroy a real protective or accountability function.

Original form

Process analysis seeks explanations for performance differences and improvement opportunities.

Problem it addressed

Explain and assess process outcomes with appropriate measures and causal limits.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Selection bias, conditioning on colliders, hidden common causes and reverse causation.

Mechanism

Distinguish description, prediction and causal intervention claims. State the proposed mechanism, plausible confounding and comparison; use stronger designs or bounded trials when an observational association could recommend the wrong intervention.

Trigger or context

A variant, actor or activity is blamed for an outcome, or a predicted association is used to choose a change.

Non trigger or cheap path

A modest reversible trial with explicit observations can be more informative than a complex causal model based on weak assumptions.

Dependencies or preconditions

A defined intervention and outcome; relevant case mix; an honest account of what identifies causation and what remains assumed.

Domain profile
Process purpose and boundary

The proposed intervention and its downstream outcome, not just observed process variants.

Beneficiaries and affected actors

People receiving the intervention and those whose performance may be wrongly blamed.

Work as described versus work as performed

Separate how work is recorded from why observed outcomes occur.

Model purpose and abstraction

Mechanism sketch, rival explanations and an appropriate comparison design.

Performance or outcome measure

Intervention-relevant outcomes with uncertainty and case-mix treatment.

Distinguish description, prediction and causal intervention claims. State the proposed mechanism, plausible confounding and comparison; use stronger designs or bounded trials when an observational association could recommend the wrong intervention.

Causal limit

S019’s causal models have explicit assumptions; S031 and S040 are associational. The retained property is restraint, not a requirement to solve all causal identification before acting.

Process owner and effective authority

Analysts can identify evidence limits; authorised owners decide on precaution, experimentation or non-intervention.

Exceptions may be responses to difficulty rather than causes of bad outcomes.

Task elimination removes non-value-adding work.

Problem it addressed

Choose a feasible intervention that changes the actual mechanism without destroying protected functions.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

A rarely used safety function disappears; undocumented error correction is mistaken for waste.

Mechanism

Before deleting a task, identify both its productive and protective functions, their consumers, and whether another mechanism preserves necessary assurance. Compare avoided effort with the error or accountability exposure created by removal.

Trigger or context

A step is labelled waste, redundant approval or avoidable checking.

Non trigger or cheap path

Retain a cheap effective check when redesign cost or uncertain risk exceeds its burden; combine duplicate checks only after their distinct functions are understood.

Hypothesis

Before deleting a task, identify both its productive and protective functions, their consumers, and whether another mechanism preserves necessary assurance. Compare avoided effort with the error or accountability exposure created by removal.

Causal limit

S016 reports practical constraints on redesign heuristics, including segregation of duties; universal elimination ignores those prerequisites.

The owner can propose deletion; the party accountable for the controlled consequence must be involved in accepting the changed exposure.

An automated check is a substitute only for the functions it actually covers.

Crosswalk worthy

True

Criterion operative coupling
Criterion

Elapsed time improves without unaccounted duplicate work, incompatible outputs or stranded partial completion.

Operating method

Execute genuinely independent activities concurrently while specifying how their outputs are joined, what happens on disagreement or partial failure, and whether resources can sustain the overlap.

Communication

Exchange readiness, completion, failure and conflicting-output information, not merely task-start notifications.

Authority

The owner arranges cross-team commitments; each performer retains authority over its own result.

Consequence evidence

Observe actual overlap, join delays and abandoned work. Measure: End-to-end lead time, resource effort, conflicting outputs and recovery.

EVOLVED_BUSINESS_PROCESS_MANAGEMENT::EBPM-029

Crosswalk worthy

True

Criterion operative coupling
Criterion

Case groups receive fit-for-purpose handling with visible misclassification and unequal-service effects.

Operating method

Separate materially different cases where this improves fit, but validate classification quality and the burdens imposed on difficult or disadvantaged cases. Reassess class boundaries when demand changes.

Communication

Recipients and performers can challenge classifications and reveal unmet needs.

Authority

Classification and resource-allocation decisions require accountable authority; analysts do not define acceptable exclusion alone.

Consequence evidence

Compare labelled classes with actual needs and outcomes. Measure: Outcomes, waiting and error by class, not only overall throughput.

Original form

Radical redesign challenges inherited work; continuous BPM sustains recurrent improvement.

Problem it addressed

Choose a feasible intervention that changes the actual mechanism without destroying protected functions.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Radicalism becomes fashion; incrementalism preserves an unworkable structure; migration is underfunded.

Mechanism

Choose the scale and pace of change by the inadequacy of the current mechanism, uncertainty, transition risk and continuity needs. Consider radical replacement, incremental repair, mixed migration and no change as genuine alternatives.

Trigger or context

The current process is being reconsidered or incremental changes repeatedly fail to address a structural problem.

Non trigger or cheap path

Retain or repair a functioning process when disruption has no warranted payoff.

Baseline understanding, transition capacity and a way to evaluate the intended consequence.

Process purpose and boundary

The process and its transition from current to proposed arrangements.

Sponsors, employees, recipients and partners exposed to disruption.

Baseline work and informal protections must be understood before replacement.

Model purpose and abstraction

Alternative and transition accounts proportionate to uncertainty.

Performance or outcome measure

Outcome improvement, transition cost, continuity and recoverability.

Redesign hypothesis and causal limit

Choose the scale and pace of change by the inadequacy of the current mechanism, uncertainty, transition risk and continuity needs. Consider radical replacement, incremental repair, mixed migration and no change as genuine alternatives.

Causal limit

S038 questions BPR novelty and unrealistic organisational claims; S027 records implementation losses rather than assuming deployment.

Process owner and effective authority

Sponsors authorise strategic disruption; performers and affected recipients contribute transition and continuity evidence.

Retain human intervention during uncertain migration.

Automation and external effect boundary

Technical deployment is only one component of organisational transition.

Failed milestones, service harm or evidence invalidating the redesign rationale.

Original form

Assign a process owner to overcome functional fragmentation.

Problem it addressed

Connect process responsibility, capability and decision authority across the relevant organisation.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Responsibility without resources; ceremonial titles; competing hierarchies; owners bypass legitimate specialist authority.

Mechanism

Connect responsibility for the process outcome with sufficient influence, knowledge, resources and an escalation route across participating functions. Separate an owner title from the powers actually exercised.

Trigger or context

An end-to-end problem crosses functional authority or an owner is assigned responsibility.

Non trigger or cheap path

In a small team, existing management and a clear escalation agreement may suffice; no extra role is required.

Dependencies or preconditions

Recognised decision rights, information access, resource commitments and a legitimate resolution path for conflicts.

Domain profile
Process purpose and boundary

The end-to-end process and the functions that control its inputs and interventions.

Beneficiaries and affected actors

Owners, functional leaders, performers, sponsors and recipients.

Work as described versus work as performed

Trace actual decisions and stalled escalations rather than relying on organisation charts.

Model purpose and abstraction

Decision-rights and escalation account, which may be a short agreement.

Performance or outcome measure

Resolved consequential decisions and resulting outcomes, not number of owner meetings.

Redesign hypothesis and causal limit
Hypothesis

Connect responsibility for the process outcome with sufficient influence, knowledge, resources and an escalation route across participating functions. Separate an owner title from the powers actually exercised.

Causal limit

S020’s field account exposes the gap between nominal and exercised ownership; S027 shows management and organisational conditions affect implementation.

Process owner and effective authority

The process owner acts within delegated powers; functional and professional authorities retain powers not transferred. Conflicts require negotiation or escalation, not fictitious unilateral control.

Human discretion and exception handling

Professional discretion and exception authorisation remain explicit.

Automation and external effect boundary

Administrative system privileges do not equal business or professional authority.

Repeated unresolved conflicts, changed scope or accountability without control.

Lineage class

NATIVE_WITH_ANALYTICAL_REFINEMENT

Original form

Align processes with organisational strategy.

Problem it addressed

Connect process responsibility, capability and decision authority across the relevant organisation.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Vague alignment language; strategy serves only powerful stakeholders; cascading targets distort work.

Mechanism

Translate strategic commitments into explicit process outcomes, selection priorities and constraints. Examine conflicts between the sponsor’s strategy, affected-party interests and actual operational capacity rather than assuming alignment is inherently beneficial.

Trigger or context

Processes compete for investment or strategic objectives change.

Non trigger or cheap path

A small service can use a few agreed outcome priorities without a formal strategy cascade.

Dependencies or preconditions

An intelligible strategy, credible operational evidence and a legitimate way to decide competing priorities.

Domain profile
Process purpose and boundary

The process portfolio and its contribution to declared commitments.

Beneficiaries and affected actors

Sponsors, operational actors and groups affected by prioritisation.

Original form

Institutionalise BPM through governance roles, structures and practices.

Problem it addressed

Connect process responsibility, capability and decision authority across the relevant organisation.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Central bureaucracy; disconnected local practice; unclear federated responsibility; governance consumes more than it protects.

Mechanism

Select centralised, decentralised or federated governance according to process interdependence, organisational context and available capabilities. Specify the decisions each arrangement enables rather than treating a BPM office as a universal requirement.

Trigger or context

Multiple units need coordination, common methods or shared process investment.

Non trigger or cheap path

Use existing management and a few explicit coordination agreements when they resolve the actual decisions.

Dependencies or preconditions

Knowledge of organisational dependencies, available competencies and the authority needed for the selected scope.

Process purpose and boundary

The organisation’s process-management decisions, not every operational act.

Beneficiaries and affected actors

Inspect actual support and decisions rather than existence of a centre or policy.

Governance configuration and interaction map at the decision level.

Performance or outcome measure

Decision effectiveness, support quality, coordination cost and process consequences.

Redesign hypothesis and causal limit

Lineage class

NATIVE_WITH_ANALYTICAL_REFINEMENT

Original form

Capability and maturity models diagnose and prescribe BPM development.

Problem it addressed

Connect process responsibility, capability and decision authority across the relevant organisation.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Gaming; self-report bias; arbitrary stages; consultant dependence; capability scores rise while outcomes deteriorate.

Mechanism

Use a capability assessment as a fallible diagnostic hypothesis about specific competencies, not as a proxy for process success or an obligatory stage ladder. Check evidence behind ratings and whether the proposed development addresses a real outcome problem.

Trigger or context

An organisation needs to diagnose capability gaps or choose improvement support.

Non trigger or cheap path

Investigate the actual failed decisions or processes directly when a broad assessment would not change action.

Dependencies or preconditions

A fit-for-purpose model, observable rating evidence, multiple relevant perspectives and an outcome-based consumer.

Domain profile
Process purpose and boundary

The assessed process-management capabilities and the outcomes they are supposed to enable.

Beneficiaries and affected actors

Assessors, managers, workers and recipients whose experience may contradict a rating.

Work as described versus work as performed

Ratings require examples of exercised capability, not policy existence alone.

Model purpose and abstraction

Dimension-specific assessment with explicit limits; a short diagnostic may suffice.

Performance or outcome measure

Actual capability use and outcomes, kept separate from the assessment score.

Redesign hypothesis and causal limit
Hypothesis

Use a capability assessment as a fallible diagnostic hypothesis about specific competencies, not as a proxy for process success or an obligatory stage ladder. Check evidence behind ratings and whether the proposed development addresses a real outcome problem.

Causal limit

S022 and S023 identify weak validation and prescriptive limits. S040 adds positive cross-sectional ESG-readiness associations but does not establish causal or environmental benefit.

Process owner and effective authority

Assessors describe evidence and limits; sponsors decide whether an identified capability warrants investment.

Human discretion and exception handling

Do not penalise justified discretion merely because it differs from a standardised procedure.

Automation and external effect boundary

Tool acquisition cannot by itself establish capability or maturity.

Feedback and revision trigger

High ratings with poor results, inconsistent raters or irrelevant prescriptions.

Expected engineering payoff
Intended postcondition

Assessment produces testable development priorities or an explicit decision that no further machinery is warranted.

Payoff status

Conditional expected payoff or rejected-claim boundary, not a universal observed effect size.

Decision or consumer
Decision

Whether and how to apply the mechanism under its trigger, or reject its universalised use. An organisation needs to diagnose capability gaps or choose improvement support.

Consumer and authority

Assessors describe evidence and limits; sponsors decide whether an identified capability warrants investment.

Actor and authority boundary

Assessors describe evidence and limits; sponsors decide whether an identified capability warrants investment.

Communication or interaction requirement

Observable postcondition

Assessment produces testable development priorities or an explicit decision that no further machinery is warranted.

Gaming; self-report bias; arbitrary stages; consultant dependence; capability scores rise while outcomes deteriorate.

Maturity is narrowed from universal progression to evidence-limited, context-specific diagnosis.

An organisation needs to diagnose capability gaps or choose improvement support.

Rigid rules cause harm; unrestricted discretion causes inconsistency, bias or untraceable decisions.

Mechanism

Distinguish legitimate discretion from uncontrolled deviation. Define the goals and constraints that remain binding, who can depart from the ordinary route, and how the decision and its consequences are communicated and reviewed.

Trigger or context

Case facts invalidate the normal route or expertise is needed beyond a fixed activity sequence.

Distinguish legitimate discretion from uncontrolled deviation. Define the goals and constraints that remain binding, who can depart from the ordinary route, and how the decision and its consequences are communicated and reviewed.

S026 criticises bureaucratic formalism; S030 raises fairness and accountability. Neither proves every workaround is legitimate.

Global property key

EVOLVED_BUSINESS_PROCESS_MANAGEMENT::EBPM-037

Crosswalk worthy

True

Criterion operative coupling
Criterion

The workaround receives an evidence-based disposition and material unresolved consequences are visible.

Operating method

Investigate a workaround’s cause, protected purpose, risks and affected parties before either suppressing it or institutionalising it. Distinguish useful repair, constraint evasion and temporary accommodation, then decide whether to change the system, the work or neither.

Communication

Connect the reason for the bypass with the people responsible for the underlying misfit and those bearing the risk.

Authority

Performers can explain the workaround; authorised owners and relevant control holders decide its acceptance or replacement.

Consequence evidence

The discrepancy itself is the evidence object; neither description automatically wins. Measure: Outcome, burden, avoided failure and new exposure caused by the workaround.

Original form

Transparency and responsible BPM make process behaviour visible and accountable.

Problem it addressed

Support legitimate human judgement while controlling unjustified deviation and harmful visibility.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Function creep, coerced consent, biased proxies, chilling of useful informal coordination and asymmetric visibility.

Mechanism

Limit process visibility and automated judgements to a declared purpose with appropriate access, participation and challenge. Examine privacy, surveillance, fairness and worker/recipient burdens as design consequences, not external afterthoughts.

Trigger or context

Monitoring, employee-level data, sensitive case information or consequential algorithmic decisions are introduced.

Non trigger or cheap path

Use aggregate, sampled or less identifying evidence when it answers the decision adequately; omit monitoring with no legitimate consumer.

A justified information purpose, proportionate access and a meaningful route for affected actors to contest error or misuse.

Preserve human challenge and avoid penalising justified exceptions mechanically.

Support legitimate human judgement while controlling unjustified deviation and harmful visibility.

Gaming, cherry-picking easy cases, premature closure, hidden rework and suppression of bad news.

Mechanism

Interpret indicators in light of the behaviour they reward, omitted work and differences in case difficulty. Use multiple relevant observations and inquiry into gaming rather than assuming the measured quantity remains a neutral description once tied to appraisal.

Trigger or context

A measure affects pay, ranking, sanctions, targets or resource access.

Use qualitative review or aggregate learning measures where precise individual attribution is not warranted.

Knowledge of incentives, case mix and how work can move outside the measurement boundary.

Compare logged attainment with case narratives and received outcomes.

An indicator-purpose-use table can be sufficient.

Outcome and distribution, including abandonment, rework and unmeasured effort.

Interpret indicators in light of the behaviour they reward, omitted work and differences in case difficulty. Use multiple relevant observations and inquiry into gaming rather than assuming the measured quantity remains a neutral description once tied to appraisal.

Implement a redesigned process through systems and organisational change.

Problem it addressed

Turn a proposed design into functioning work with accountable external effects.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Technically live but unused system; abandoned implementation; shadow work; disruption of necessary informal coordination.

Mechanism

Treat enactment as the joint establishment of working technology, roles, skills, resources, coordination and actual adoption. Verify that actors can perform the intended work and that the organisation receives the outcome; deployment is only one observation.

Trigger or context

A to-be design is introduced or a new system is claimed to improve a process.

Non trigger or cheap path

An organisational agreement, training or information change may suffice without new software.

Dependencies or preconditions

Operational readiness, integration with surrounding work, accountable authority and an evaluation baseline.

Domain profile
Process purpose and boundary

The redesigned process and the surrounding organisation that must make it work.

Beneficiaries and affected actors

Performers, technical/support teams, recipients and dependent organisations.

Work as described versus work as performed

Observe real use and off-system work instead of equating installation with adoption.

Model purpose and abstraction

Readiness and actual-case evidence, with models suited to the change.

Performance or outcome measure

Adoption, completion, lead time, errors, burden and transition cost.

Redesign hypothesis and causal limit
Hypothesis

Treat enactment as the joint establishment of working technology, roles, skills, resources, coordination and actual adoption. Verify that actors can perform the intended work and that the organisation receives the outcome; deployment is only one observation.

Causal limit

S027 followed 25 intended processes but only seven implemented processes were evaluated; selection and concurrent change limit benefit claims.

Process owner and effective authority

Sponsors resource change; owners coordinate adoption; technical teams control only technical deployment within their mandate.

Human discretion and exception handling

Actors need practical means to handle unexpected cases during migration.

Automation and external effect boundary

Executable workflow is a component, not the organisational process itself.

Feedback and revision trigger

Non-use, unresolved cases, workaround growth, adverse outcomes or withdrawal of needed support.

Expected engineering payoff
Intended postcondition

Real cases are completed under the new arrangement with responsibilities and observed consequences understood.

Payoff status

Conditional expected payoff or rejected-claim boundary, not a universal observed effect size.

Decision or consumer
Decision

Whether and how to apply the mechanism under its trigger, or reject its universalised use. A to-be design is introduced or a new system is claimed to improve a process.

Consumer and authority

Sponsors resource change; owners coordinate adoption; technical teams control only technical deployment within their mandate.

Actor and authority boundary

Sponsors resource change; owners coordinate adoption; technical teams control only technical deployment within their mandate.

Performers, support staff, partners and recipients exchange readiness, problems and unresolved work during transition.

Known failure modes

Technically live but unused system; abandoned implementation; shadow work; disruption of necessary informal coordination.

Important criticisms

S027 followed 25 intended processes but only seven implemented processes were evaluated; selection and concurrent change limit benefit claims.

How the property evolved

Implementation success is separated from design quality, installation and subsequent outcome improvement.

Mature or evolved form

Treat enactment as the joint establishment of working technology, roles, skills, resources, coordination and actual adoption. Verify that actors can perform the intended work and that the organisation receives the outcome; deployment is only one observation.

Ceremony vs property
Protected function

Real cases are completed under the new arrangement with responsibilities and observed consequences understood.

Consumer

Minimal adequate alternative

An organisational agreement, training or information change may suffice without new software.

Fuller form trigger

Prerequisites

Simplification risk

Omission or retirement condition

Omit when the stated trigger is absent, an existing/cheaper mechanism supplies the required function, or its risk/consumer/dependency has disappeared. Reconsider on: Non-use, unresolved cases, workaround growth, adverse outcomes or withdrawal of needed support.

Anti ceremony boundary

Presence of an artefact, role, meeting, score or tool does not establish the observable postcondition; removing it must not destroy a real protective or accountability function.

Fragile screen automation, accelerated flawed decisions, hidden exceptions and maintenance cost omitted from benefit claims.

Select automation according to process stability, interface characteristics, data quality, exception load and the value of human judgement. Compare interface-level RPA, deeper integration and non-automation; test the actual changed work rather than relying on a tool category.

Repetitive digital work or coordination overhead suggests a technical intervention.

Criterion operative coupling
Criterion

Declared completion corresponds to the agreed business outcome, or remaining uncertainty and responsibility are explicit.

Operating method

Distinguish a local task or engine completion from completion of the obligation to a recipient or partner. Identify the external effects that matter and obtain appropriate receiving-side or operational evidence before declaring the business case complete.

NATIVE_WITH_ANALYTICAL_REFINEMENT

Original form

Process execution and case management provide exception, cancellation and recovery constructs.

Problem it addressed

Turn a proposed design into functioning work with accountable external effects.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Blind retry duplicates effects; a stop leaves recipients stranded; nominal rollback cannot undo human or external consequences.

Mechanism

Where failed or interrupted work can leave consequential partial effects, ensure actors know how to pause, assess outstanding obligations and select an authorised continuation or recovery. The BPM-level requirement does not prescribe engine-specific retry, rollback or compensation algorithms.

Trigger or context

Work can fail after consequential action or unsafe continuation is plausible.

Non trigger or cheap path

For a reversible low-impact task, manual stop-and-check with a responsible person may be sufficient.

Dependencies or preconditions

Visibility of partial work, reachable responsible actors and feasible recovery options.

Domain profile
Process purpose and boundary

Partial cases, external effects and their outstanding responsibilities.

Operators, recipients, partners and authorised recovery decision-makers.

Work as described versus work as performed

Record actual partial effects, including those missing from the normal log.

Model purpose and abstraction

A recovery/continuity account proportional to consequence and reversibility.

Performance or outcome measure

Unresolved cases, harm prevented or caused by stopping, and recovery outcome.

Redesign hypothesis and causal limit
Hypothesis

Where failed or interrupted work can leave consequential partial effects, ensure actors know how to pause, assess outstanding obligations and select an authorised continuation or recovery. The BPM-level requirement does not prescribe engine-specific retry, rollback or compensation algorithms.

Causal limit

The inspected specifications establish modelling/execution constructs, not universal organisational recovery success; S027 demonstrates limits of deployment evidence.

Process owner and effective authority

Operators may stop within delegated authority; reversal or compensation of another actor’s commitment requires the relevant authority.

Human discretion and exception handling

Provide a practical route for manual judgement on ambiguous failures.

Automation and external effect boundary

Technical cancellation does not imply reversal of an external business effect.

Failed observation, partial completion, unsafe continuation or exhausted recovery options.

Mechanism

Reassess models, assumptions and measures when demand, case mix, resources, interfaces or actual practices change. Distinguish benign variation from a changed mechanism and avoid updating the model merely to normalise a harmful deviation.

Trigger or context

Observed patterns differ materially from the baseline or the operating environment changes.

Versioned assumptions and comparative case evidence; no mandatory full model refresh.

Known failure modes

Important criticisms

S018 demonstrates technically richer simulation but does not remove future-demand uncertainty; S025’s workarounds are contextual rather than universal drift diagnoses.

How the property evolved

Lifecycle feedback is retained as selective assumption review, not perpetual automatic redesign.

Mature or evolved form

Reassess models, assumptions and measures when demand, case mix, resources, interfaces or actual practices change. Distinguish benign variation from a changed mechanism and avoid updating the model merely to normalise a harmful deviation.

Ceremony vs property
Protected function

The change is classified and consequential assumptions or controls are reviewed with reasons.

Consumer

Analysts identify changed evidence; owners and affected actors decide whether models, operations or objectives need revision.

Minimal adequate alternative

A focused review of changed cases may suffice; continuous automated drift detection is unnecessary for infrequent stable work.

Fuller form trigger

Observed patterns differ materially from the baseline or the operating environment changes.

Prerequisites

A stated baseline and scope, relevant observations and knowledge of environmental changes.

Simplification risk

Drift detector chases noise; a new normal embeds harm; stale resource assumptions invalidate simulation.

Omission or retirement condition

Omit when the stated trigger is absent, an existing/cheaper mechanism supplies the required function, or its risk/consumer/dependency has disappeared. Reconsider on: Demand/resource change, new workaround pattern, interface revision or outcome drift.

Anti ceremony boundary

Presence of an artefact, role, meeting, score or tool does not establish the observable postcondition; removing it must not destroy a real protective or accountability function.

Make observations capable of informing action and differentiated revision.

Self-confirming metrics, inaccessible complaint channels, cherry-picked external evidence and excessive investigative burden.

Mechanism

Keep a route by which observations outside the current model—complaints, practitioner accounts, recipient experience and unlogged work—can challenge both the representation and the success measure. Do not let the model define all admissible evidence about its own adequacy.

Trigger or context

A process is evaluated primarily through records generated by its existing model or system.

The process plus the boundary defining what its model and measures can observe.

Contradiction between work and representation is admissible evidence, not automatically a defect in the worker.

Model purpose and abstraction

A discrepancy account and revised inquiry; a larger formal model is not always the answer.

Performance or outcome measure

Omitted burden, unresolved complaints and whether model-based decisions remain warranted.

Negotiate shared outcomes, interfaces, responsibilities and dispute handling among autonomous organisations. Make differences in incentives, information and decision rights explicit; no single process diagram grants one participant authority over the network.

Trigger or context

A received outcome depends on independent organisations with their own commitments.

Negotiate shared outcomes, interfaces, responsibilities and dispute handling among autonomous organisations. Make differences in incentives, information and decision rights explicit; no single process diagram grants one participant authority over the network.

Criterion operative coupling
Criterion

A sustainability claim states what changed, for whom, over which boundary and with what evidence limits.

Operating method

Include material environmental and societal consequences in process purpose, boundaries and redesign comparisons. Identify who or what bears these effects and distinguish measured outcomes from reporting capability, commitments or maturity ratings.

Explain impact assumptions, displaced burdens and conflicts rather than announcing all objectives simultaneously improved.

Authority

Sponsors and owners decide within legitimate constraints; affected parties and domain experts contribute consequences that internal metrics may omit.

Consequence evidence

Inspect actual consumption and consequences, not only sustainability procedures or self-reports. Measure: Material environmental/social outcomes separately from reporting capability.

Original form

Agentic BPM proposes autonomous planning, enactment and adaptation of processes.

Problem it addressed

Coordinate autonomous actors and new capabilities without overstating authority, effectiveness or impact.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Self-authorisation, goal misspecification, cascading external effects, unverifiable improvement and loss of meaningful human control.

Mechanism

Candidate proposition: agents could revise and enact organisational processes under goals and constraints. The inspected 2026 manifesto formulates research requirements; this study does not establish that autonomous cross-context self-revision is safe, effective or adequately governed.

Trigger or context

An agent is proposed to choose and execute consequential process changes without case-by-case human approval.

Non trigger or cheap path

Use bounded assistance, recommendations or explicitly delegated reversible operations while retaining authorised review of consequential redesign.

Dependencies or preconditions

Validated authority boundaries, observability, evaluation, continuity, security and affected-party accountability would be required; the corpus does not show a general solution.

Domain profile
Process purpose and boundary

Trace actual decisions and stalled escalations rather than relying on organisation charts. Measure: Resolved consequential decisions and resulting outcomes, not number of owner meetings.

Problem it addressed

Make the relationships among otherwise useful BPM mechanisms coherent rather than assuming their conjunction automatically works.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Analysis without agency; authority without warrant; action without benefit; excessive documentation of trivial links.

Mechanism

Keep three linked but non-equivalent claims explicit: evidence supports a distinction about work; an identified actor is authorised and able to intervene; observed consequences support an outcome judgement. Require the missing link to be established before promoting one claim into another.

Trigger or context

A model, analytic result or recommendation is proposed as sufficient justification for operational change or success.

A small team can establish the links through a short case discussion, an existing decision-maker and direct outcome confirmation.

The process plus the evidence-to-action-to-consequence relations used to manage it.

A relational account with optional compact records, not a forced sequential workflow.

Crosswalk worthy

True

Criterion operative coupling
Criterion

A claim of improvement can be traced through warranted observation, an actual authorised intervention and its observed result, with missing links explicit.

Operating method

Keep three linked but non-equivalent claims explicit: evidence supports a distinction about work; an identified actor is authorised and able to intervene; observed consequences support an outcome judgement. Require the missing link to be established before promoting one claim into another.

Communication

Transfer the evidence, uncertainty and proposed action to the responsible actor, then return consequence evidence to the original judgement.

Authority

Evidence producers do not acquire execution powers by analysis; authorised actors do not acquire factual correctness by holding office.

Consequence evidence

Evidence of a model, a decision and an outcome are separately observed; none substitutes for the others. Measure: The original process outcome and whether each inferential/operative link is actually established.
