Original form

Analytical composition of end-to-end boundaries, plural measures, redesign comparison and external accountability.

Problem it addressed

Make the relationships among otherwise useful BPM mechanisms coherent rather than assuming their conjunction automatically works.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Infinite scope expansion, strategic nondisclosure, metric aggregation masking harm and excessive evaluation cost.

Mechanism

Accept an improvement claim only over its declared consequence boundary and protected outcomes. A local gain remains qualified when material receiving-side burdens are unknown; do not aggregate away a harmed group or silently change the boundary to rescue the claim.

Trigger or context

A redesign appears beneficial on one unit’s measures or changes who bears work and risk.

Non trigger or cheap path

For a simple isolated process, recipient confirmation and a small burden check may suffice.

Dependencies or preconditions

Explicit affected-party scope, comparable outcomes and a legitimate adjudicator of unavoidable trade-offs.

Domain profile
Process purpose and boundary

The intervention and materially affected consequences, with explicit exclusions.

Beneficiaries and affected actors

Beneficiaries, workers, partners and parties bearing displaced effort, risk or environmental effects.

Work as described versus work as performed

Receiving-side and off-system evidence can challenge local records.

Model purpose and abstraction

A consequence-boundary and trade-off account rather than one scalar score.

Performance or outcome measure

Outcome and burden by affected party, with uncertainty retained.

Redesign hypothesis and causal limit

Accept an improvement claim only over its declared consequence boundary and protected outcomes. A local gain remains qualified when material receiving-side burdens are unknown; do not aggregate away a harmed group or silently change the boundary to rescue the claim.

This is an analytical acceptance condition, not evidence that all costs can be measured or all values reconciled.

Process owner and effective authority

The party claiming benefit cannot unilaterally accept another party’s material burden as harmless.

A justified exception may preserve a protected outcome despite lowering throughput.

Automation and external effect boundary

Automated throughput gains cannot conceal scaled harm or external repair work.

Displaced burden, scope change, new affected party or contradictory outcome evidence.

Expected engineering payoff

Problem it addressed

Make the relationships among otherwise useful BPM mechanisms coherent rather than assuming their conjunction automatically works.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

False economy removes needed evidence; simplicity becomes dogma; overlapping controls are removed without understanding defence or accountability functions.

Mechanism

Select the smallest set of BPM mechanisms that jointly covers the actual purpose, evidence, authority and feedback needs. Evaluate shared functions and dependencies before adding artefacts, roles or tools; omit or retire machinery whose function is already adequately supplied or no longer needed.

Trigger or context

A BPM method, model, role, assessment or platform is proposed, expanded or retained.

Non trigger or cheap path

The management machinery used for the selected process, not the whole organisation by default.

Beneficiaries and affected actors

Method consumers, performers, decision-makers and those paying coordination/documentation costs.

Work as described versus work as performed

Evaluate exercised functions rather than artefact presence.

Model purpose and abstraction

The lightest adequate representation for its users and decisions.

Performance or outcome measure

Protected outcomes and total coordination/evidence cost.

Original form

Analytical composition of discovery, enactment, monitoring and revision.

Problem it addressed

Make the relationships among otherwise useful BPM mechanisms coherent rather than assuming their conjunction automatically works.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Model laundering of bad practice; uncommunicated process change; evaluation criteria rewritten to declare success; loss of continuity.

Mechanism

Allow feedback to change a representation, the real work, the measure or the intervention hypothesis, but distinguish these acts. Review their consistency and continuity: updating a diagram does not change work, and changed work may require a revised account without implying improvement.

Trigger or context

Consequences or exceptions challenge the current process account or a revision is proposed.

Non trigger or cheap path

A local correction to a note may suffice when work and authority are unchanged; avoid reopening the entire portfolio for a representational typo.

Dependencies or preconditions

Identified mismatch, actors authorised for the relevant kind of change and evidence of affected dependencies.

Domain profile
Process purpose and boundary

The process, its representations, measures and current change commitments.

Beneficiaries and affected actors

Performers, modellers, owners, evaluators, recipients and partners affected by revision.

Work as described versus work as performed

Maintain the distinction between altered accounts and altered practice.

Model purpose and abstraction

Version and purpose relationships sufficient for affected consumers, not mandatory elaborate configuration machinery.

Performance or outcome measure

Actual outcome, continuity and whether the revised account remains warranted.

Redesign hypothesis and causal limit
Hypothesis

Allow feedback to change a representation, the real work, the measure or the intervention hypothesis, but distinguish these acts. Review their consistency and continuity: updating a diagram does not change work, and changed work may require a revised account without implying improvement.

Causal limit

This synthesis is not a claim that BPM methods are automatically self-authorising or that feedback converges to a globally optimal process.

Process owner and effective authority

Modellers may revise descriptions within their remit; changing operational commitments or evaluation criteria requires the responsible authority.

Human discretion and exception handling

Recurring exceptions can trigger redesign, but each departure is not automatically a new standard.

Automation and external effect boundary

A model update must not silently become permission for automated external action.

Important criticisms

S042 supplies formal reasoning and prototype evidence, not general deployment validation. S014 highlights the challenge of evolving knowledge-intensive contexts.

How the property evolved

Constraint-based flexibility is retained with explicit composition and change-consistency obligations, separated from the representation-selection property EBPM-016.

Mature or evolved form

Where the chosen formalism supports it, check that the combined constraints admit appropriate executions and that a changed instance specification remains compatible with its recorded history. Separate formal satisfiability and dead-activity checks from the truth, completeness and legitimacy of the encoded constraints.

Ceremony vs property
Protected function

Within the checked formal model, the stated consistency/history-compatibility result holds; no claim about unencoded harm or real-world correctness follows.

Consumer

Analysts check encoded behaviour; accountable domain actors decide which constraints should apply and whether a departure is authorised.

Minimal adequate alternative

For a few transparent constraints, competent manual checking may suffice; procedural or case-based alternatives may be easier for the actual users.

Fuller form trigger

A declarative process has interacting constraints or is changed while cases are in progress.

Prerequisites

A defined event alphabet and trace semantics, correct encoding, adequate history and a tractable analysis method.

Simplification risk

Omitted obligations; wrong event mapping; satisfiable but harmful behaviour; state-space/constraint complexity; missing actual history.

Omission or retirement condition

Omit when the stated trigger is absent, an existing/cheaper mechanism supplies the required function, or its risk/consumer/dependency has disappeared. Reconsider on: Added/changed constraint, conflicting obligation, instance migration or unreliable history.

Anti ceremony boundary

Presence of an artefact, role, meeting, score or tool does not establish the observable postcondition; removing it must not destroy a real protective or accountability function.
